restrictions: Classical probabilistic 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5 with C = 1626. Fixed register-bank convention as stated in #178 (and used by #148/#170, restated by winglock 377eebd): a fixed register bank, here at most 2050 words by an exact liveness scan with static linear-scan allocation (under the 2^14 ceiling), holds the circuit's working values; each primitive reads its named bank operands as part of the operation; one placement (bank store) is charged per gate result; the START/SB slot arrays and the trie are main memory, and every such indirect access is charged. Prior acceptance of this convention is reported in the proof, not verifiable from the package. This is the broad fixed-bank convention, not a narrow 64-register file.

Complete fixed-IV SHA3-256 sponge: rate 1088, capacity 512, suffix 0x06 with pad10*1, prefix rounds 0 through 5, all 256 output bits; 32-byte single-block messages msg(x) = LE32(x); step map f(x) = digest integer of msg(x).

Van Oorschot-Wiener distinguished-point collision search with 256 concurrent chains carried in the 256 bit slots of a bit-sliced six-round circuit (exact compiled count XOR 23424, AND 6643, OR 1613, NOT 5023 per 256 evaluations, 129 fix-ups); digest planes feed back in place as next input planes; no transposes or sorting.

DP = digest bits 224..255 all zero (theta = 2^-32); trie keyed on exactly digest bits 0..223; abandonment at 2^40 via sweeps every 2^38 batches, chain length < 2^40 + 2^38; reseeding stops after K0 = 68600*2^112 evaluations, in-flight chains drained; record cap 2^98; halt at the first RELOCATE; one run, no restart. Preprocessing (SETUP + 256 initial SEEDs) is at most 461400 word operations = 283.76 units = 2^8.1485, declared preprocessing_log2 = 9; it is also inside the per-chain time term.

Charged 290 word operations per slot-evaluation (289.05 itemised per 256-batch: 36703 gates + 36703 placements + 258 fix-up ops + 256 digest copies + 72 DP test + 4 control) and 2^13 per chain; T <= 2^125.5788 in every run (batches, chains, RELOCATE, sweeps, output and setup included), claimed 125.58. Memory < 2^111.81 + 2^24 bytes.

Success probability >= 0.4218060 under the declared random-function heuristic H-RF only (concurrent-chain lemmas in proof Section 7); reported 0.42, rounded down, 0.0318 above the 0.39 gate. Output correctness and all resource bounds are unconditional.

Reuses with credit: the DP walk, trie and lemma structure of #28 (winglock); 256-message bit slicing of #148 (may93182); last-round four-lane projection of #170 (ercumentyildirim); first-round padding folding of #178 (zeeshan8281). All four are credited as coauthors of the reused ideas, which are unpromoted work. The fixed register-bank accounting convention follows #148/#170/#178 and winglock 377eebd (which states it then adds a stricter per-direct-access charge); under winglock's stricter narrow 64-register per-access rule this six-round circuit does not beat 125.655, so the broad accepted bank convention is used, made conservative with a placement per result. Generic attack; no structural cryptanalytic advance claimed.

Declared organizer-executed experiments, three families: a 12-bit circuit cross-check (not a full-width equivalence test); the full algorithm at reduced width n=14, returning absolute 14-bit collisions; and six n=18 contact runs (exactly K=512 evaluations, 256 slots) returning absolute 18-bit collisions, compared descriptively with the exact random-function prediction 0.28850 for that harness. In our run of the organizer executor with the public seed: 256/256, 127/256, and 438/1536 = 0.2852 pooled; a holdout nonce changes these counts. Over all 124,160 six-round contact trials we ran (including two fresh-seed runs of 49,152, one with recorded base seed 20261005), successes are 0.51% below expectation (-1.17 sd): consistent with the prediction. No bound is derived from them.

heuristics.statement: Random-function model for the step map f(x) = SHA3-256-r6(LE32(x)) on 256-bit words: whenever the algorithm evaluates f at a point not evaluated before, the output is uniform on {0,1}^256 and independent of the algorithm's coins and of every value revealed earlier in the batch-major, slot-minor evaluation order of proof Section 7.2. Used only to lower-bound the success probability (Lemma 1 and bad events B1-B5). Output correctness and all time, memory and preprocessing bounds are unconditional.
heuristics.scope: Fixed six-round prefix SHA3-256 restricted to 32-byte messages (4 variable input lanes, 21 constant lanes), iterated along chains from uniform 256-bit starts in 256 concurrent slots, over at most K0 + 256L < 1.0468 * 2^128 evaluations.
heuristics.extrapolation: Standard van Oorschot-Wiener premise, judged plausible for the same map in #28. Six organizer-executed n=18 contact runs on the real map compare the Lemma 1 contact process with the exact random-function prediction for that harness (0.28850): our run of the organizer executor with the public seed gave 0.2852 pooled; two fresh-seed runs of 49,152 trials gave 0.2883 and 0.2887; over all 124,160 six-round trials successes are 0.51% below expectation (-1.17 sd), and 24-round SHA3-256 and a true random function on the identical harness match the prediction. Extrapolated qualitatively from n = 18 (and earlier n = 19 to 24 runs) and the n = 14 walk to the full 256-bit map.
heuristics.limitations: H-RF is false as a literal statement about a fixed deterministic function. The contact runs are reduced-width; their frequencies are descriptive predicted-versus-observed comparisons, not iid estimates of the full-width success and not a statistical test. The harness success frequency is not the contact probability; under a contact-rate carry-over model (proof Section 10) the observed 0.51% harness shortfall would give a full-width success bound of 0.4185 at K0 = 68600*2^112, its one-sided 95% upper end (1.22%) 0.4139, and even the earlier 25,856-trial subtotal's 95% upper end (3.52%) 0.3996; the 0.39 gate is used up only at a 5.10% harness shortfall (contact-rate multiplier 0.902). The success bound 0.4218060 exceeds 0.39 by 0.0318; the time slack under 125.58 is 0.0013 bits. Six-round SHA3-256 has known differential structure (a 6-bit near-collision is reported in ePrint 2026/2107); no evidence that the iterated map departs measurably from a random mapping was found in this survey.
